dossier.public_summary: The dips are twice as deep on even transits as odd (4.4x) and vary from missing to 2600 ppm between sectors, which a planet cannot do. A secondary eclipse is also seen, and the detections alternate and even vanish. The signal is an eclipsing binary on the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by nearly a factor of 4.4 at 12.06 sigma, the classic signature of an eclipsing binary at twice the period (period_x2 27.6). All sectors show the same odd/even sign (sector_oe_sectors_over_3: 2, sector_oe_same_sign_share 0.75).

Depth is not steady; it truly changes within one pipeline. sector_depths_by_source verdict is changes_within_a_source with p_constant_all 3.739e-97, consistent with alternating eclipses disappearing in some sectors rather than aperture calibration.
reasons.value: p_constant 1.029e-97, depth_change_pct 298.3 per_sector: -78 ppm, 1543 ppm, 2646 ppm, -55 ppm, 510 ppm

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent, with nine measured events and the top three carrying 99.3% of the signal, as nondetections and deep eclipses alternate rather than a repeating planet transit.
reasons.value: p_consistent 6.707067586433845e-233, share_of_top_3 0.993, outliers 2949 ppm and 3477 ppm vs -78 ppm, -55 ppm, -33 ppm

reasons.why: A second dip is detected at snr 5.66 near phase 0.5255 with a stellar-like depth ratio, well above the brightest bump, as expected for a bound EB, despite its proximity to a strong spot modulation.
